Sam Park: Hey folks — quick flag: our holiday calendar marked 2026-08-30 as the observed day for the Ireland office but managers had communicated 08/29. A couple people ended up with PTO deducted twice. @people-ops? :thinking:
Jordan (People Ops): Ugh, thanks for flagging. Can you DM me the employee IDs and the affected dates? We need manager sign-off to reverse per audit rules.
Sam Park: Pasting HRIS export (sanitized):
- eid:30122 Mae O. — PTO used 2026-08-30, observed holiday 2026-08-29
- eid:30123 Tom B. — PTO used 2026-08-30, observed holiday 2026-08-29
- eid:30124 Ira K. — PTO used 2026-08-30, observed holiday 2026-08-29
Lina (Payroll): Looping payroll ops. Looks like a calendar normalization edge-case for locales with bank-holiday observance. We can queue reversals once manager approval is posted. Command we'll run:
```bash
python hr_tools/reconcile_holidays.py --rollback --ids 30122,30123,30124 --region IE --note "observed-shift-aug2026"
```
Rory (Manager): Confirmed — I approve reversals for those three employees. Please proceed. :thumbsup:
Lina (Payroll): Rolled back duplicate PTO deductions and updated HRIS balances. Added detection rule HR_HOL_021 to flag observed-date mismatches during calendar syncs. Changes will show on the next payroll run.
Jordan (People Ops): Thanks — I'll update the time-off FAQ and create an internal how-to for managers to request reversals (audit steps included). Opening incident HR-2026-231 for records.
Sam Park: Balances look correct now in the portal. Appreciate the quick response :clap:
